outcomes research into real-world effectiveness is useful for policymakers to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of novel therapies in daily practice but that its usefulness for generating robust evidence on effectiveness is limited due to the challenges of conducting outcomes research in daily practice.
outcomes research into the effectiveness of a novel therapy in daily practice can be useful for policymakers in the re-assessment of a conditional reimbursement decision.
outcomes research is useful for addressing to whom bortezomibi was administered in daily clinical practice, but is limited in generating robust evidence of its real-world safety and efficacy.

the usefulness of outcomes research in Dutch daily practice to inform the re-assessment of novel therapies in the context of conditional pricing and reimbursement.
the usefulness of outcomes research for evaluating novel therapies in daily practice and its limitations for policymakers.
the usefulness of real-world evidence for outcomes research and its role in reimbursement decisions.

real-world evidence on the effectiveness of novel drugs is often of poor quality, which may limit its usefulness for policymakers in the re-assessment period.
